messages:
ashley: Hey team — had a medical emergency while hiking in Idaho last week and they airlifted me to Regional Air Med. I just got an EOB showing the air ambulance billed as out-of-network and patient responsibility is $9,200. I'm on Redwood PPO Gold. This feels like a surprise bill?

sam_people_ops: Oh no, glad you're ok. Short answer: emergency air transport can be messy. First: are you stable and home now? Second: did you get copies of the bill + incident report?

ashley: Back home and recovering, thanks. I have the ambulance invoice (lists "Regional Air Med" TIN), the hospital intake note, and the crew report. EOB: denial code "provider not contracted" and patient balance $9,200.

broker-julia: Many states have surprise-billing protections that apply for emergency transport. I'll open a case with Acme and flag for surprise-bill review. Can you DM me the invoice and the hospital's emergency note? Also need member last4 2246.

ashley: DM sent with docs and last4.

insurance-bot: Case created: ACME-AMB-202609-7701. Status: awaiting provider billing details and clinical notes.

emergency-billing: Hi Ashley  this is Regional Air Med billing. Sorry for the stress. We billed per usual; we can provide an itemized statement and proof of medical necessity. We can also check if our billing office can reissue using the hospital's admitting TIN for bundling.

sam_people_ops: Broker-Julia, two parallel asks: 1) request Acme to apply state surprise-billing rules / emergency balance-billing protections, 2) ask provider to refile or attach hospital rendering NPI if applicable. I'll note internal support if short-term assistance is needed.

broker-julia: On it. ACME-AMB-202609-7701 updated: I requested surprise-billing escalation and submitted clinical docs. Also asked Acme to confirm whether the air ambulance is treated as emergency and therefore eligible for in-network-equivalent payment.

insurance-bot: ACME-AMB-202609-7701 updated: network ops acknowledged escalation; requested provider invoice and crew report.

emergency-billing: Uploaded crew report and itemized bill to the insurer portal and added hospital admit note linking service to emergency. Reference SR# RAM-INV-4432.

ben-hr: Ashley, filing a note in our benefits tracker. If Acme confirms insurer liability but pays slowly, we can offer a short-term expense advance through the benefits exceptions fund. Let us know if you want that option.

ashley: Appreciate it but hoping insurer handles it. I don't want extra debt.

insurance-bot: ACME-AMB-202609-7701 closed: adjudicated as emergency service; processed at in-network-equivalent rate per state surprise-billing protections. Member responsibility adjusted to $150 copay. Reimbursement/payment posted to provider. Notification emailed to member.

broker-julia: Closing loop: Acme applied surprise-billing protections; provider accepted in-network equivalent payment. Verified final EOB shows $150 copay. Case closed.

ashley: Thank you everyone  huge relief. Appreciate the quick help and the advance offer. :heart:
